headline.purpose: Names the current primary workspace without becoming a marketing hero.

title.purpose: Dialog, record, and focused section titles.

body.purpose: Explanatory prose and longer evidence summaries.

body-compact.purpose: Dense queue, control, and record copy.

label.purpose: Buttons, fields, navigation, and actionable row text.

data-label.purpose: Table headings, metric axes, and compact fact names.

mono.purpose: Local paths, identifiers, and code values only.

shadows.name: structural-rest
shadows.purpose: Barely visible lift for top-level panels, selected navigation, and buttons.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Dialogs only, against the overlay scrim and without a decorative border.

shadows.name: sticky-separation
shadows.purpose: Separates the anchored review decision bar from scrolling evidence.

shadows.name: mobile-navigation-lift
shadows.purpose: Separates the fixed mobile navigation from the active workspace.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Button, field, selection, and overlay state changes.

motion.name: loading-spin
motion.purpose: Continuous rotation for the compact loading indicator only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Collapses animation and transition duration when reduced motion is requested.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single action that advances the current decision.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 36px; padding: 7px 12px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; border: 1px solid var(--accent); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: white; background: var(--accent); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); font-size: 0.84rem; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 120ms ease, background-color 120ms ease, box-shadow 120ms ease; } .ds-button-primary:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--accent-hover); background: var(--accent-hover); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button-primary:active:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-button-primary:disabled { color: var(--ink-faint); border-color: var(--border); background: var(--surface-subtle); box-shadow: none; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A safe, reversible action that remains visible without competing with the primary decision.
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 36px; padding: 7px 12px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--ink); background: var(--surface); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); font-size: 0.84rem; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 120ms ease, background-color 120ms ease; } .ds-button-secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--border-strong); background: var(--surface-subtle); } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button-secondary:active:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-button-secondary:disabled { color: var(--ink-faint); background: var(--surface-subtle); box-shadow: none; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: A low-emphasis utility for dismissal, pagination, or tertiary actions.
components.css: .ds-button-ghost { display: inline-flex; min-height: 36px; padding: 7px 12px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--ink-muted); background: transparent; font-size: 0.84rem; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 120ms ease, color 120ms ease; } .ds-button-ghost:hover:not(:disabled) { color: var(--ink); background: var(--surface-subtle); } .ds-button-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button-ghost:active:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-button-ghost:disabled { color: var(--ink-faint); cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: A destructive or explicitly negative outcome control.
components.css: .ds-button-danger { display: inline-flex; min-height: 36px; padding: 7px 12px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid oklch(0.85 0.07 28); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--danger); background: var(--danger-soft); font-size: 0.84rem; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 120ms ease, background-color 120ms ease; } .ds-button-danger:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--danger); background: oklch(0.93 0.05 28); } .ds-button-danger:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button-danger:active:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-button-danger:disabled { color: var(--ink-faint); border-color: var(--border); background: var(--surface-subtle); cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Labeled Text Input
components.description: A persistent label, compact control, and constraint hint for research and settings forms.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: var(--ink-muted); font-size: 0.81rem; font-weight: 620; } .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 38px; padding: 7px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--ink); background: var(--surface); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px oklch(0.2 0.02 275 / 0.025); font-size: 0.84rem; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-muted); } .ds-input:hover { border-color: oklch(0.68 0.035 275); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.8 0.09 280 / 0.7); outline-offset: 0; border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-input:disabled { color: var(--ink-faint); border-color: var(--border); background: var(--surface-subtle); cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-field small { color: var(--ink-muted); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 450; }

components.name: Review Checkbox
components.description: A compact binary filter or explicit owner confirmation with a visible text label.
components.css: .ds-checkbox-field { display: inline-flex; min-height: 28px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: var(--ink-muted); font-size: 0.81rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; } .ds-checkbox { width: 18px; height: 18px; margin: 0; border-radius: 4px; accent-color: var(--accent); cursor: pointer; } .ds-checkbox-field:hover { color: var(--ink); } .ds-checkbox:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-checkbox:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.55; }

components.name: Semantic Status Badge
components.description: A plain-language state label paired with a semantic tonal treatment.
components.html: Verified
components.css: .ds-badge-success { display: inline-flex; min-height: 22px; padding: 3px 7px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 4px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.83 0.07 154); border-radius: 999px; color: oklch(0.38 0.1 154); background: var(--success-soft); font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Primary Navigation Item
components.description: A familiar destination link with icon, text, and an explicit active state.
components.html: Discover
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; min-height: 40px; padding: 9px 10px; align-items: center; gap: 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--ink-muted); background: transparent; font-size: 0.83rem; font-weight: 610; text-decoration: none; transition: color 120ms ease, background-color 120ms ease, border-color 120ms ease; } .ds-nav-item:hover { color: var(--ink); background: oklch(0.985 0.006 275); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-item.is-active { color: var(--accent-ink); background: var(--surface); border-color: var(--border); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); }

narrative.overview:
RecruitAI should feel like a well-organized research desk used for hours at a time: light, quiet, compact, and explicit about what needs attention. Cool violet-tinted neutrals separate the fixed navigation, working canvas, queues, and record surfaces without turning every region into a floating card. One restrained violet action color creates a clear path through discovery, review, and outreach.

The interface is a workbench, not a campaign. Lists stay dense enough to scan, then open into one reusable workspace where evidence, people, conflicts, and history can be inspected without losing queue position. Semantic colors communicate state alongside plain-language labels and icons. Motion is brief and functional; automation proposes, while the owner remains visibly in control.

The system explicitly rejects bloated enterprise CRM density, sales-engagement gamification, dark neon “hacker” styling, generic AI gradients, glassmorphism, spreadsheet replicas, novelty controls, and multi-step wizards. Familiar interaction patterns and progressive depth are the design advantage.
keyCharacteristics: Compact queue-and-workspace layouts with one obvious next action.
Cool near-white tonal layers with violet reserved for action and current context.
Evidence states expressed through color, icon, label, freshness, and source.
One sans-serif family, tight hierarchy, and data-friendly labels.
Local-first and human-reviewed safeguards made visible in the interface.
Responsive structure that collapses navigation and swaps queue/workspace views without hiding capability.

rules.name: The One-Decision Rule
rules.body: Every surface must make the next useful decision visually obvious; secondary controls recede until they are needed.

rules.name: The Progressive-Depth Rule
rules.body: Keep queues compact and reveal full record context in the adjacent workspace or one focused dialog. Never expose every stored field at once.

rules.name: The Ten-Percent Violet Rule
rules.body: Decisive Violet occupies no more than roughly 10% of a screen. Its scarcity tells the owner where to act.

rules.name: The Evidence-Is-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red, and blue appear only when a real record state exists. Always pair them with an icon, label, or both.

rules.name: The Readability Rule
rules.body: Use Graphite Ink or Muted Graphite for meaningful copy. Faint Graphite is prohibited for placeholders, instructions, and any text the owner must read to complete a task.

rules.name: The One-Voice Rule
rules.body: Use one sans-serif family across headings, controls, labels, and data. Never introduce a display font for product UI.

rules.name: The Quiet-Metadata Rule
rules.body: Metadata may be smaller, but it must remain readable. If a timestamp or source label carries a decision, promote it to Compact Body and Muted Graphite.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A resting surface earns either a border or a shadow based on its structural role. Never combine a 1px border with a wide decorative shadow.

rules.name: The State-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Use 120–140ms transitions for hover, focus, selection, and dialog entry. Loading rotation is the sole continuous animation. Reduced-motion preferences collapse all movement to an immediate state change.

dos: Do keep one obvious primary action per decision region and use Decisive Violet only for action, current selection, or focus.
Do place source, freshness, conflict, and verification evidence beside the fact it qualifies.
Do use the queue-and-workspace pattern to preserve context while reviewing one company bundle at a time.
Do pair semantic color with a plain-language label, icon, or both.
Do keep focus rings visible at 3px and preserve keyboard order through navigation, queues, tabs, dialogs, and decision controls.
Do keep compact desktop controls at least 36px high and mobile navigation targets at least 44px high.
Do use full borders, background tints, and tonal layering to show selection and hierarchy.
Do retain empty, loading, error, disabled, and completed states for every workflow.
Do keep all data, credential, local-only, and send-safeguard messaging candid and close to the affected action.
donts: Don't create bloated enterprise CRMs with deep configuration trees and duplicate concepts.
Don't turn the product into a sales-engagement dashboard that gamifies activity volume instead of showing evidence quality.
Don't use dark neon “hacker” styling, generic AI gradients, glassmorphism, or novelty interfaces.
Don't build spreadsheet replicas that expose every field at once and make review feel like data entry.
Don't introduce multi-step wizards for actions that can be completed in one clear screen.
Don't use a colored `border-left` or `border-right` greater than 1px as a selected-row, card, notice, or callout stripe; use a full outline or tonal fill.
Don't pair a 1px border with a shadow blur of 16px or more on the same surface.
Don't use gradient text, decorative grid backgrounds, repeating stripe backgrounds, or ornamental glass effects.
Don't apply green, amber, red, blue, or saturated violet to inactive states or for decoration.
Don't use Faint Graphite for placeholders, instructions, or required decision context.
Don't hide uncertainty behind a single score; show the underlying evidence, age, and conflicts.
Don't use decorative motion, orchestrated page-load sequences, bounce, or elastic easing.
Don't reinvent native form, dialog, tab, navigation, or scrolling affordances for personality.
